market_context: US equity futures indicate a sharp relief rally after the worst weekly selloff, with S&P 500 futures up roughly 2.6%-2.9%, Nasdaq-100 futures up about 3.0%-3.6%, and Dow futures up roughly 1.5%-2.1%. Nvidia was reported up more than 8% premarket after falling 23% last week, while Treasury yields rebounded toward 4.94%-4.96%; the calendar is light, with commercial paper and H.15 interest-rate releases listed and investors watching a New York Fed president's remarks.

predictions.reasoning: S&P 500 futures were up approximately 2.6%-2.9% before the open after seven consecutive declining sessions and a correction-level selloff. The broad-market relief signal supports a substantial rebound from the $689.81 baseline, although higher Treasury yields may limit the advance.

Nasdaq-100 futures were reported up roughly 3.0%-3.6%, led by a sharp premarket recovery in battered AI and semiconductor shares. That momentum favors a strong rebound in QQQ after its 10.5% five-day decline, though the target assumes some giveback from the futures move.

Nvidia was reported up about 8.2%-8.3% premarket after losing approximately 23% the prior week, making it a central driver of the relief rally. The extreme oversold condition and renewed AI-stock buying favor further gains, but profit-taking could keep the close below the initial premarket impulse.

The reported rebound is concentrated in high-beta technology and AI-linked shares, a backdrop that generally supports Tesla after its 7.64% prior-session loss and 11.4% five-day decline. Because the available news specifically highlights semiconductors rather than Tesla, the expected gain is more modest and confidence is lower.
